# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Jan 13, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing CI processes with weekly upgrade test block updates and adding JWT authentication to the op-interop-filter admin API. Significant work was also done on contract test improvements and the removal of L2OutputOracle support.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### CI/CD and Testing Enhancements
Improvements were made to the CI pipeline, including a new feature to update upgrade test blocks weekly, ensuring more current testing environments ([#18634](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18634)). A fix was also implemented to address issues with `solc` installation during contract tests ([#18753](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18753)). Additionally, `MintManager` tests were converted to fuzz tests for broader coverage ([#18744](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18744)).

### Interoperability and Security Updates
The `op-interop-filter` now includes JWT authentication for its admin API, enhancing security for administrative functions ([#18771](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18771)).

### Protocol Simplification and Upgrades
Support for the L2OutputOracle has been removed from the `op-proposer` to simplify its logic ([#18706](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18706)). The project also saw an upgrade to `op-geth` ([#18767](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18767)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
Six new pull requests were opened today, focusing on various enhancements and features:
- [#18777](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18777) proposes making the sealing duration value configurable in `op-node`.
- [#18776](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18776) introduces a flag to enable the interop supervisor in `op-node`.
- [#18775](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18775) adds a `depset` package for interop dependency set management in `op-service`.
- [#18772](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18772) adds historical proof support for the devstack.
- [#18769](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18769) introduces route-specific JWT authentication support in `op-service`.
- [#18768](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18768) is a feature to run U18.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Dispute Monitoring and Challenger Integration
The issue related to displaying new multi-node metrics in the `dispute-mon` dashboard has been closed, indicating completion of the Grafana dashboard update ([#18205](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18205)). The integration of a supernode provider into the challenger has also been completed and closed ([#18524](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18524)).

### Upgrade and Protocol Simplification
The finalization of U18 releases has been completed ([#18548](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18548)). Additionally, the task to remove L2OutputOracle support from the `op-proposer` has been closed, simplifying the proposer's logic ([#18620](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18620)).

### OP Reth Enhancements
The issue concerning the addition of batcher throttling to OP Reth has been closed ([#18747](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18747)).

## NEW ISSUES

### OP Reth and Forge Deployer Development
Several new issues have been opened concerning `op-reth` feature parity, including batcher throttling ([#18763](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18763), [#18764](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18764)). New issues also address the Forge Deployer, focusing on creating a default flag for its use, fixing `op-e2e` tests with parallel `op-deployer` instances, and removing old OPCM code ([#18761](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18761), [#18760](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18760), [#18762](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18762)).

### Kona and CI Improvements
New issues include a review of Kona derivation ([#18765](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18765)) and the extraction of `op-core` from `op-geth` ([#18766](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18766)). CI improvements are also being tracked, specifically simplifying `kona-proof`'s CI using Kona's monorepo and implementing dynamic config with path-filtering for conditional CI job execution ([#18773](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18773), [#18774](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18774)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### CI Dynamic Configuration and Kona Integration ([#18774](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18774))
Discussion revolves around leveraging CircleCI's dynamic config and path-filtering to conditionally run CI jobs, particularly for Kona. A key point raised is the dual use of `kona/version.json` for both acceptance tests and `kona-host` releases within the `op-challenger` docker image. The ideal scenario is for `kona-host` to be released as part of `op-challenger` to ensure consistency, avoiding confusion if separate `Kona-host` releases don't align with what's included in `op-challenger`.
